summary: Show, find and install emulators portably
description: Shows the emulators that VintageCoder uses (VICE, atari800, Altirra, Xemu, Fujisan), with homepage, license and role. `install` downloads a fixed version from the project's site, only when you call it explicitly. It checks the SHA-256 sum and unpacks it below VintageCoder (`emulators/<Emulator>/<Version>` in the configuration folder). Nothing is shipped and nothing is downloaded without this call.

forms.summary: show the emulators of the catalog with homepage and role
show what is found (all sources) and what can be installed

args.name: emulator
args.help: ID (vice, atari800, altirra, xemu, fujisan) or variant (x64sc, x128 ...). Without it, all.

notes: The automatic order is: path from the settings, otherwise what PATH and the usual program folders offer, and last the newest portably installed version.

forms.summary: download a fixed version, check it and install it portably

args.name: emulator[@version]
args.help: ID (vice, atari800, altirra, xemu, fujisan) or variant (x64sc, x128 ...), optionally with a version (vice@3.9). Without a version, the default (the newest) is used.

options.help: Only shows the package, address, checksum and target folder, without downloading anything.

notes: Uses `curl` and `tar` of the system (Windows 10/11 and Linux include them). Where there is no portable package (e.g. macOS, VICE on Linux), the command names the download page.
If the version is already installed, nothing happens. If the checksum does not match, the file is deleted and nothing is unpacked.
In the automatic search, portably installed programs come after PATH and the usual program folders. A path in the settings and a version chosen with `@version` take priority.

Several versions of an emulator can exist side by side. `vcc emulator status` shows all sources found (portable and system) and the versions that can be downloaded. `vcc test --backend vice@3.9` uses a specific one.
